hypothesis: Adding a dedicated data and tooling RCA subsystem that instruments ingestion, embedding, indexing, retrieval, and tool invocations will (a) detect and correctly localize at least 80% of induced data and tool failures within 5 minutes and (b) reduce the median time to identify root cause (MTTR-rca) for user-visible errors by at least 50% compared to a metrics-only observability baseline.

baseline.description: LLM RAG and tool-using application with standard observability (infrastructure metrics, basic logs, and request-level traces) but no specialized RCA subsystem for data, retrieval, or tooling. On-call engineers rely on ad-hoc dashboards and manual log inspection.

components.llm_gateway: HTTP API that accepts user queries, orchestrates RAG retrieval and tool calls, and returns responses.

rag_pipeline.document_store: Relational or object store containing source documents.
rag_pipeline.embedding_service: Service that generates embeddings for documents and queries.
rag_pipeline.vector_index: Vector database or index used for nearest-neighbor retrieval.

tooling_layer.tool_registry: Static configuration of tools and their endpoints.

logs: Tool invocation logs with status codes
Retriever logs with query and hit count
traces: Distributed traces for each user request, including spans for retrieval and tool calls

rca_capabilities.data_pipeline: No explicit tracking of ingestion runs, data freshness, or embedding/index versions; only coarse job status metrics (success/failure).
rca_capabilities.retrieval: No retrieval quality metrics (e.g., recall, coverage, relevance); only raw hit counts and latency.
rca_capabilities.tooling: Tool failures visible only via error logs and generic error-rate metrics; no structured cause categorization or correlation to user-visible incidents.
rca_capabilities.user_correlation: No automated correlation between user-visible failures and upstream data or tool events; triage is manual.

treatment.description: Baseline system augmented with a specialized RCA subsystem for data, retrieval, and tooling. The subsystem consumes structured events from ingestion, embedding, indexing, retrieval, and tool layers; computes retrieval health metrics; detects anomalies; and correlates user-visible failures with upstream incidents.

instrumentation.ingestion_jobs: Emit structured events for job_start, job_complete, job_failure, and per-batch stats (rows_processed, rows_failed, source_version, target_index_id).
instrumentation.embedding_pipeline: Emit events for embedding_batch_processed with document_ids, embedding_model_version, success_count, failure_count, and latency distribution.
instrumentation.indexing_process: Emit index_snapshot events capturing index_id, corpus_version, doc_count, last_update_ts, and shard_status.
instrumentation.retriever: Emit retrieval_query events with query_id, user_request_id, query_text_hash, top_k, retrieved_doc_ids, retrieval_score_stats, and index_version.
instrumentation.tool_invocations: Emit tool_call events with tool_name, version, input_schema_hash, status (success, timeout, 4xx, 5xx, logical_error), latency_ms, and response_summary_hash.

event_pipeline.transport: Streaming bus (e.g., Kafka or Redis Streams) topic 'rca.events.data_tooling'.
event_pipeline.schema_registry: JSON schema or Avro schemas for job, embedding, indexing, retrieval, and tool events.
event_pipeline.collector: Python service that normalizes events into a unified RCA event model and writes to a time-series store and document store.

retrieval_health_analyzers.drift_detection: Jobs that compare current retrieval metrics (recall proxy, coverage, relevance scores from an evaluator) to a rolling baseline and raise anomalies.
retrieval_health_analyzers.coverage_monitor: Track per-namespace or per-dataset coverage and freshness (document counts, last_update_ts).

tooling_health_analyzers.tool_error_classifier: Classify tool_call failures into categories (network, timeout, auth, schema_mismatch, semantic_error).
tooling_health_analyzers.flakiness_detector: Compute rolling error rate and error burst patterns per tool endpoint and emit flakiness_incident events when thresholds or patterns are triggered.

linking_logic: Link user_request events to retrieval_query and tool_call events via correlation_ids.
Attach the latest ingestion_job, embedding_pipeline, and index_snapshot metadata to each retrieval_query.
Cluster user-visible failures by common upstream attributes (index_version, ingestion_job_id, tool_name, tool_endpoint).

rca_alerts.data_incident_alerts: Emit alerts when a job failure correlates with a spike in retrieval misses or content-related user failures.
rca_alerts.tool_incident_alerts: Emit alerts when a tool becomes flaky, along with impacted user_request_ids and failure summaries.

workloads.name: WL1-normal-mixed-traffic
workloads.description: Baseline mixed workload of RAG and tool-using requests with healthy ingestion, retrieval, and tools.

rag_queries: AskQuestionsAboutDocs(query='What are the support SLAs for product Z?')
combined_rag_plus_tool: Use RAG to find latest maintenance window docs, then call calendar tool to check conflicts.

workloads.name: WL2-broken-ingestion-job
workloads.description: Simulate a broken ingestion job that silently stops updating a subset of documents for the RAG corpus, leading to stale or missing content while the system continues serving.

symptoms: No new documents ingested after T0 for affected_namespace
ingestion_job reports 'success' (for the baseline, no structured error emission)
user queries for newly added policies return outdated answers or missing content

workloads.name: WL3-flaky-tool-endpoint
workloads.description: Simulate a flaky external tool/API used by the LLM agent that intermittently fails with timeouts and transient 5xx errors.

symptoms: User-visible responses that omit tool-based data or return fallback text.
Increased latency for requests requiring the tool.
Elevated error rates and retries for the tool endpoint.

controls.experimental_design: A/B-style within-environment runs comparing baseline vs treatment under identical workloads and injected failures.

constants.llm_model: Same LLM model version, configuration, and provider used for both baseline and treatment.
constants.rag_corpus: Same underlying document set, same schema, and same initial index snapshot.
constants.tools: Same tool APIs, endpoints, rate limits, and failure injection patterns.
constants.traffic_replay: Deterministic or recorded workload generator with fixed random seeds and identical request sequences for baseline and treatment.
constants.infrastructure: Same hardware/VM shapes, network configuration, and deployment topology.
constants.time_window: Experiments run within a short time window to minimize background environment drift.

independent: Presence or absence of the data and tooling RCA subsystem (instrumentation, analyzers, correlation engine).
Injected failure types and timing (broken ingestion, flaky tool).
dependent: Time to detect data or tool incidents.
Time to correctly localize root cause.
Detection rate and precision for induced failures.
Volume and quality of RCA alerts.

replication.note: Repeat WL2 and WL3 three times each for baseline and treatment to account for stochasticity in LLM outputs and network variability.

metrics.name: incident_detection_latency_data_pipeline
metrics.description: Elapsed time between the actual injection of the ingestion failure in WL2 and the first automated detection signal/alert indicating a data or ingestion-related issue.

metrics.name: incident_detection_latency_tooling
metrics.description: Elapsed time between the start of tool flakiness in WL3 and the first automated detection signal/alert indicating a tool or API health issue.

metrics.name: rca_localization_time_data_pipeline
metrics.description: Elapsed time between user-visible symptom onset for WL2 (first failed or stale-answer request) and the generation of an RCA artifact that points to the ingestion/indexing subsystem as the primary root cause.

metrics.name: rca_localization_time_tooling
metrics.description: Elapsed time between user-visible symptom onset for WL3 and the generation of an RCA artifact that identifies the specific tool and endpoint as the primary root cause.

metrics.name: detection_recall_induced_incidents
metrics.description: Fraction of induced incidents (ingestion breaks and tool flakiness episodes) that are detected by the system as incidents of any severity.

metrics.name: detection_precision_incident_alerts
metrics.description: Fraction of generated incident alerts (classified as data or tool related) that correspond to real induced incidents (excluding benign anomalies and noise).

metrics.name: localization_accuracy
metrics.description: Fraction of detected incidents for which the RCA output correctly identifies the primary failing component (e.g., specific ingestion job or tool endpoint).

metrics.name: mean_user_visible_error_rate
metrics.description: Average fraction of user requests during failure phases that result in user-visible errors or degraded responses (e.g., fallback messaging, stale content). Used mostly for contextualizing incident impact.

metrics.name: rca_event_volume
metrics.description: Rate of RCA-related events (instrumentation events plus RCA alerts) to evaluate overhead and signal volume between baseline and treatment.

metrics.name: rca_processing_overhead
metrics.description: Additional processing latency added to user requests by RCA instrumentation and correlation logic, measured as the difference in median end-to-end latency between baseline and treatment under WL1.

primary.scope: Across WL2 and WL3 for treatment runs; no minimum required for baseline.
Median across treatment runs (5 minutes or less).
Median across treatment runs (5 minutes or less).
Ratio between treatment and baseline medians for WL2.
Ratio between treatment and baseline medians for WL3.
Treatment runs combining WL2 and WL3.

secondary.scope: Treatment runs; ensures alerts are not excessively noisy.
Treatment vs baseline median latency difference under WL1 (<= 20 ms per request).

interpretation_notes: If primary criteria are met but secondary criteria fail (e.g., precision or overhead is worse than target), the subsystem is effective but needs tuning before production deployment.
If detection_recall_induced_incidents is low but localization_accuracy is high, consider improvements in anomaly thresholds and upstream signal coverage.
If localization_accuracy is low despite high detection_recall, correlation logic or schema coverage is likely insufficient.

failure_modes.name: undetected_ingestion_failure
failure_modes.description: The ingestion break in WL2 does not trigger any data-related incident alert in the treatment condition.
failure_modes.impact: Stale or missing content persists undetected, undermining the premise of the data RCA subsystem.
mitigations: Verify that ingestion jobs emit events to the RCA bus and that schemas match expectations.
Lower anomaly detection thresholds for data freshness and index_version changes.
Add explicit SLIs for document freshness and corpus coverage per namespace.

failure_modes.name: mislocalized_ingestion_root_cause
failure_modes.description: An incident is detected in WL2 but RCA blames the LLM model or prompt configuration rather than the ingestion/indexing layer.
failure_modes.impact: Engineers may pursue ineffective remediations, delaying the real fix.
mitigations: Improve correlation rules to prioritize signals from ingestion failures temporally aligned with symptom spikes.
Enhance retrieval metrics and metadata to make index_version and corpus_version changes more salient.
Incorporate retriever-level quality probes (known-answer queries) as an additional signal.

failure_modes.name: undetected_tool_flakiness
failure_modes.description: The induced flakiness in WL3 does not cause any tool-related incident alert in the treatment condition.
failure_modes.impact: User-visible errors from tools remain unexplained and require manual triage.
mitigations: Ensure tool_call events are correctly emitted and ingested for both successes and failures.
Adjust flakiness detection thresholds and time windows for error-rate anomalies.
Include error-burst detection (e.g., consecutive failures) as a separate signal.

failure_modes.name: false_positive_incident_alerts
failure_modes.description: The RCA subsystem raises frequent data- or tool-related incident alerts even during WL1 normal operation.
failure_modes.impact: On-call fatigue and distrust of RCA outputs.
mitigations: Tune anomaly detection thresholds and require multiple confirmatory signals (e.g., combining error rate and user-visible symptom rate).
Introduce alert aggregation and suppression logic for low-severity anomalies.
Incorporate a baseline learning period before enabling high-severity alerts.

failure_modes.name: excessive_rca_overhead
failure_modes.description: RCA instrumentation and processing adds significant latency or resource consumption.
failure_modes.impact: Degrades user experience and increases infrastructure costs.
mitigations: Sample high-volume event streams while maintaining coverage for critical paths.
Move heavy analysis to asynchronous jobs rather than request inline flows.
Profile RCA services and optimize serialization, batching, and storage access.

failure_modes.name: schema_drift_in_rca_events
failure_modes.description: Event schemas change between runs, breaking parsers or correlation logic and invalidating comparisons between baseline and treatment.
mitigations: Use schema registry with versioning and explicit compatibility checks.
Pin RCA subsystem and application code to specific commits for the experiment.
Include schema_version fields in all events and assert expected versions in tests.

infrastructure.compute: At least 3 nodes or VMs (or equivalent containers): one for the application (LLM gateway + RAG + tools), one for observability and storage (metrics + logs + RCA store), and one for the RCA subsystem and workload generator.
infrastructure.network: Stable internal network with predictable latency; ability to simulate network issues for tools if desired.

storage.rca_store: Document database (e.g., PostgreSQL, MongoDB, or S3-compatible object store) for RCA events and artifacts.
storage.vector_db: Any vector database used by the RAG pipeline (e.g., FAISS, Milvus, pgvector).

dependencies: FastAPI or Flask for the LLM gateway and tools.
Async task framework (e.g., asyncio, Celery, or similar) for background jobs.
Kafka client or Redis client for event streaming.
OpenTelemetry SDK for instrumentation (optional but recommended).

data.rag_corpus: Synthetic document corpus for the domain (e.g., support policies and product docs) with at least 1,000 documents across multiple namespaces.
data.ingestion_scripts: Scripts to populate document store and build baseline vector indices pre-experiment.
data.ground_truth_queries: A small set of canonical queries with known relevant documents used to approximate recall and coverage metrics during WL2.

run_instructions.title: Clone repository and set up environment
notes: Ensure any additional experiment-specific dependencies listed in experiments/11/requirements.txt are installed if present.

run_instructions.title: Provision and configure observability and RCA backing services
commands: # Start local Prometheus, vector DB, and event bus via docker-compose
notes: Alternatively, point configs to existing Prometheus, vector DB, and Kafka/Redis deployments in your environment.
Verify connectivity using provided health-check scripts in scripts/healthchecks/.

run_instructions.title: Bootstrap RAG corpus and indices
notes: These scripts should populate the document store and create the initial embedding and index snapshots used for WL1–WL3.
Record the initial index_version emitted by the tooling for later verification.

run_instructions.title: Deploy baseline application stack (without RCA subsystem)
notes: Ensure that only standard metrics/logging instrumentation is enabled.
Confirm that no RCA-specific event streams (e.g., rca.events.data_tooling) are being consumed.

run_instructions.title: Run baseline workloads WL1, WL2, WL3
notes: Each workload config should specify the failure injection schedule and random_seed.
Repeat runs for each workload with different seeds (e.g., 42, 43, 44) by passing --seed=<value>.
During WL2 and WL3, ensure the failure injection scripts for ingestion and tool flakiness are invoked as configured.

run_instructions.title: Collect baseline metrics and RCA artifacts (if any)
notes: At baseline, RCA-specific metrics (detection and localization) will likely be absent or set to sentinel values; these will serve as a comparison point for the treatment.
Export Prometheus time-series for the experiment window if needed for fine-grained analysis.

run_instructions.title: Deploy treatment application stack (with RCA subsystem)
notes: Confirm that ingestion, embedding, indexing, retrieval, and tool components are emitting RCA events to the event bus.
Verify RCA service health endpoints before running workloads.

run_instructions.title: Run treatment workloads WL1, WL2, WL3
notes: Use the same seeds as in baseline runs to ensure comparable request sequences.
Monitor log output from services/rca_data_tooling to confirm incident detection and RCA artifacts are being generated.

run_instructions.title: Collect treatment metrics and RCA artifacts
notes: RCA artifacts should include timestamps for detection and localization, as well as structured root-cause summaries.
Confirm that the number of detected incidents aligns roughly with the known induced incidents.

run_instructions.title: Compute experiment-level summary metrics and compare baseline vs treatment
notes: This script should compute medians and distributions for detection and localization times, detection recall, precision, localization accuracy, and overhead.
No interpretation should be hard-coded; the summary is purely descriptive. You will interpret against success_criteria manually or in a separate notebook.

experiment_id.description: ID of the experiment, must match 'exp-11-data-retrieval-tooling-rca-v1'.

runs.description: Per-run metadata and raw measurements for baseline and treatment.

run_id.description: Unique identifier for this specific run.

seed.description: Random seed used for the workload generator.

incident_ground_truth.description: List of induced incidents and their ground-truth properties for this run.

component.description: Name or identifier of the failing job, index, or tool endpoint.

incident_detections.description: RCA or monitoring system incident detections for this run.

linked_ground_truth_incident_id.description: If this detection can be matched to a ground-truth induced incident, record its ID; else null.

metrics.description: Per-run raw metrics (before aggregation across runs).

metrics_summary.description: Aggregated metrics across runs for baseline and treatment.

baseline_vs_treatment_ratios.description: Computed ratios to compare baseline and treatment for key metrics.

rca_artifacts.description: Sample RCA outputs for representative incidents (for qualitative inspection).

linked_incident_id.description: ID of the ground-truth incident this artifact pertains to, if applicable.

root_cause_summary.description: Human-readable summary generated by the RCA subsystem (e.g., via templates or LLM).

items.description: Identifiers for underlying events, logs, metrics, or traces used to produce this RCA artifact.
